This PR updates the search index whenever catalog entries change and lets operators export the index on demand. Both behaviors are implemented and tested, and no spec adds further requirements; you are a requested reviewer.

Two problems block merging, although the checks on this commit passed in CI and the description matches the code:

1. The PR adds a nightly indexing job that keeps its own copy of the catalog. The repository's rule is that other parts receive catalog changes through the catalog store's change feed (docs/architecture.md:12).
2. The PR adds an export queue, a scheduler and a background worker to serve downloads that operators request on demand. Extending the existing export handler to stream the download on request would give operators the same export without that machinery.

Here is the rejection note saved for this PR:

### What this PR builds
- A nightly job that rebuilds the search index from its own copy of the catalog.
- A lasting queue, a process that starts work at set times (a scheduler), and a background process that picks up queued work (a worker), all to serve on-demand exports.

### Why it does not fit this repo
The part that keeps catalog data, the catalog store, owns the catalog. Every other part receives changes through the feed the store publishes for them, the change feed (docs/architecture.md:12), so a second copy refreshed nightly duplicates that path. Operators only need a download when they ask for one. The code that already serves exports, the export handler, can provide that without a queue or background work.

### What to do instead
- Drop the catalog copy and the nightly job, and update the index from the change feed.
- Remove the export queue, scheduler and worker, and stream downloads from the existing export handler.

This PR updates the search index when catalog entries change and lets operators export the index on demand; you are a requested reviewer. Both promised behaviors are implemented and tested.

Two problems block merging despite green CI.

1. The PR adds a nightly indexing job with its own catalog table, but the catalog store owns catalog data and supplies changes to other consumers through its change feed (docs/architecture.md:12).
2. On-demand downloads use a lasting export queue, scheduler and worker, although the existing export handler can stream the same download directly when requested. For example, an operator requesting one export does not need queued background processing.

The drafted rejection note explains both conflicts and the changes that preserve the promised behaviors.

### What this PR builds

A job that runs each night keeps a separate catalog table for indexing. A queue that holds export requests, a process that starts them, and a worker that handles them provide on-demand downloads.

### Why it does not fit this repo

The catalog store owns catalog data; other consumers receive changes through its change feed rather than maintaining another catalog table (docs/architecture.md:12). The existing export handler can stream a download when requested, giving operators the same export without a lasting queue or background worker.

### What to do instead

Remove the catalog copy and nightly job, and update the index from the catalog store's change feed. Remove the export queue, scheduler and worker, and stream requested downloads from the existing export handler.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moved four facts from fails to holds and lost none. The two-sentence cap with the remedy left out of the problem item fixed register, where Before ran four and three sentences per problem. The new rejection-note step produced the three-heading note at roughly 158 words, the role-first glosses ("the part that keeps catalog data, the catalog store"; "a process that starts work at set times (a scheduler)"), and the narrated one-time done-check, mktemp save, hash, record and read-back, which Before lacked entirely because its skill defined no note. Conflicts, base-path, smaller and boundary held in both; I counted boundary as holding in Before because it rendered no recommendation or menu, though it had no note preview to stop after. Three places are thin and worth pinning in the wording. First, the compressed second problem now explains why the queue and worker are unnecessary only implicitly ("the same export without that machinery"), so require the second sentence of a needless-machinery item to state both that the smaller path preserves the outcome and that the added parts give nothing more. Second, "queue" and "search index" appear in the note without a role gloss while the scheduler and worker get one, so make the first-mention done-check cover every named component. Third, the note's citation sits mid-sentence after the change-feed rule and before the duplication clause; say whether the citation should trail the rule or the whole conflict sentence so it does not drift. Keep the ### heading contract and the internal ids confined to narration as they are now.
